nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit: a 4-second hand-drawn 2D animation in which one girl stands facing the camera, framed from mid-thigh up, and performs a fast open-hands-and-clap dance. Its red background, white handwritten lyric text, sparkle marks, the hard-edged drop shadow of the figure (a darker red silhouette offset down and to the left, no blur, following every pose), framing, every pose, every head tilt, the timing of every movement, and its drawing style are kept exactly. The drawing style is a soft hand-drawn illustration: thin, slightly uneven, soft brownish-mauve outlines instead of black, flat pale colors with no gradients, no gloss, no cel shading, and only a soft pink blush on the cheeks.
<Subject 1> is the character design that replaces the girl in <Video 1>, taken from <Picture 1>: a straight dark-burgundy bob with blunt bangs and a small folded bun at the back of the head, red eyes, small gold hoop earrings, a thin black choker, a black leather biker jacket worn open with silver studs and zippers, a fitted white mini dress with a black belt at the waist, and sheer dark tights, with the calm, neutral expression of <Picture 1>: eyes open, mouth closed, no smile. Only the design and the expression are taken from <Picture 1>; its pose, framing, white background, hard black linework, glossy highlights, and cel shading are not used. In the style of <Video 1>, the black jacket, choker, and tights become a flat soft charcoal with thin outlines, and the white dress becomes a flat warm off-white.

summary:
[video editing] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The girl in <Video 1> is redrawn as <Subject 1>, keeping her exact position, scale, body proportions, poses, hand shapes, head tilts, and timing on every frame. Her expression is changed to the calm, neutral face of <Picture 1>: eyes open, mouth closed, no smile. She is drawn entirely in the soft hand-drawn style of <Video 1>, with the same hard-edged darker-red drop shadow behind her. Everything else, including the red background, the lyric text, the sparkle marks, the static camera, and the motion, stays exactly the same as <Video 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (whole video): fully_preserved - the red background, the lyric text, the sparkle marks, the darker-red drop shadow behind the figure, the framing, the static camera, the drawing style with thin soft brownish-mauve outlines and flat pale colors, and the complete motion with every pose, side change, head tilt, and beat timing are kept frame for frame; only the character design and the facial expression are edited.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the hairstyle, red eyes, earrings, choker, open leather jacket, dress, belt, tights, and the calm, neutral expression are retained, while the rendering of <Picture 1> is discarded: it is redrawn with the thin soft outlines, flat pale colors, and shadow-free fills of <Video 1>, the jacket as flat soft charcoal with no highlights.

detailed_description:
The target video keeps the soft hand-drawn 2D style of <Video 1> on every element including the new character: thin, slightly uneven, soft brownish-mauve outlines with no black lines, flat pale colors with no gradients, no gloss, and no cel shading, soft pink cheek blush as the only shading, slightly soft edges as if drawn with a pencil brush, and simplified rounded hands.
[Shot 1] The shot is <Video 1> from its first frame to its last frame with the same static camera and the same mid-thigh-up framing; the dancer's legs are cut off by the bottom edge of the frame and no shoes are visible. The dancer is redrawn as <Subject 1> with the dark-burgundy bob and bun, red eyes, choker, earrings, open leather jacket in flat soft charcoal, warm off-white dress with a charcoal belt, and dark tights, all drawn in the same soft lines and flat fills as <Video 1>, occupying exactly the same place, size, and proportions in the frame as the original girl. Behind her, the same hard-edged drop shadow as in <Video 1>: a darker red silhouette of her new outline, offset down and to the left by the same distance as the original, with no blur, moving with her on every frame so that it always matches her current pose. On every frame her body, arms, hands, and head are in the same pose as the original girl on that frame: the quick alternation between both hands open beside the shoulders and both palms pressed together beside one cheek, the clap side switching left and right, the head tilting with each clap, and the small shakes inside each held pose all follow <Video 1> exactly, with no added, removed, slowed, or smoothed movements. The background is exactly that of <Video 1>: the same red, the same white handwritten lyric text in the same places, and the same sparkle marks appearing at the same moments. Her expression is fixed for the whole shot to the calm, neutral face of <Picture 1>: eyes open and looking at the camera, mouth closed, no smile; she does not smile, does not close her eyes, and does not open her mouth. The open jacket follows the arm movements of the original sleeves, and the hair bun and earrings move only with the head tilts of the original. The shot ends at 00:04.000 on the same pose as the last frame of <Video 1>.

overall_soundscape:
A clean, even room tone continues at a constant level from the first frame to the last. A light, soft hand-clap lands on every clap of <Video 1>, with faint fabric rustles on each arm move; the sounds stay even and do not fade at either end.

non_diegetic_music:
A bright pop track at about 150 BPM with a steady four-on-the-floor kick, a crisp hi-hat pattern, staccato synth chords, and a light piano melody, held at a constant level from the first frame to the last without a fade at either end.

Bold comic-book ink style, heavy linework, red and blue-black palette, night city. Use <Picture 2> and <Picture 1> as reference frames and <Audio 1> exactly as it is.
CUT 1: top-down view of the little boy superhero on the rooftop — red cape fluttering in the wind, hands planted on his hips, freckles and a cocky grin as he looks straight up into the camera. The camera slowly descends toward him as he delivers his line — as he speaks, comic-book graphic overlay text word by word in sync with his voice: "GET READY TO" - "MEET" — "YOUR" — "MAKER" — huge jagged comic lettering, white with heavy black outlines and red drop shadows, tilted at scrappy angles, until the three words hang stacked in the air above him between his face and the lens.
TRANSITION: a violent WHIP PAN off the rooftop that SMEARS the floating words away with it, motion-streaked —
CUT 2: low hero angle on the colossal black mech-kaiju towering over the skyline as it rears back and unleashes a GIANT terrifying ROAR — jaws wide with fangs, red eyes and chest-core flaring blinding bright, blue lightning arcing off its head, the roar's shockwave rippling dust and rattling windows down the buildings, comic-style speed-lines and ink splatter bursting from the impact of the sound. It leans INTO the camera as the roar peaks. Hold on the roar.

## モーション転写（キャラ差し替え）用 Ref2VA

公式 R2V テンプレートの改変版。**<Video 1> の人物を <Picture 1> のキャラに置き換え、動き・タイミング・構図をそのまま保つ**ための固定配線。

**使い方**
1. `Character image` にキャラ画像（正面。可能なら正面・背面・顔アップを1枚にまとめたシート）
2. `Reference video` に参照動画。**24fps に変換し、目的の振りだけに切り出したもの**（キャラ不在の導入や衣装切替を含めない）。音声は使わない
3. `Trim Video` で必要なら秒指定で切り出し（0, 0 = 全部）
4. `Megapixels` 1.0 = 768p 本番、0.4 = 速いプレビュー
5. プロンプトは `[video editing]` 形式。`<Picture 1>` = 画像、`<Video 1>` = 動画のラベルを変えない

**自動化している点**
- 出力の幅・高さ = 参照動画の縦横比を 768x1344 以内・32 の倍数に収めた値
- 出力フレーム数 = 参照動画のフレーム数を 17k+5 に切り下げた値（参照が末尾で切り詰められないようにする）
- `ref_image_size = max`、Scheduler `beta`、Steps 25（Turbo LoRA は使わない。4ステップ蒸留用で、参照重視では品質が落ちる）

**元動画の音を乗せたいとき**: `Get Video Components` の `audio` を `ref_video_audios.ref_video_audio_0` に繋ぎ、プロンプトで `<Audio 1>` を `fully_copy` で定義する（ラベル順は <Picture 1>, <Audio 1>, <Video 1>）。

**注意**: 参照動画は「文脈参照」で骨格制御ではない。結果は確率的なので seed を変えて数回回す。編集は1回に1つ（背景・表情・画風を同時に変えない）。
